answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on a signed attestation graph, where each honest seed contributes limited influence. A sybil cluster with few external edges has low conductance, φ = cut(S,¬S)/vol(S); thus only limited walk probability can enter it, bounding its aggregate voting weight by the boundary flow rather than its claimed population. Juniper nodes may relay a signal, but a cipher-backed identity alone adds no trust.
